title: Self-XSS Chained via CSRF
learning_objectives: Understand why 'self-XSS' is dismissed as low-severity — a bio rendered raw only on the owner's own /profile can only run script in your own session
Turn self-XSS into account takeover by chaining CSRF: if the state-changing endpoint that sets the bio has no CSRF token, an attacker page can plant the payload in the VICTIM's profile

Recognise that a state change exposed over GET is CSRF-able by a top-level navigation, and that SameSite=Lax cookies ARE sent on cross-site top-level GET navigations (but NOT on cross-site POST) — so the GET update carries the admin's session
Chain the two: CSRF plants the self-XSS in the admin's bio, the redirect renders it raw in the admin's own session, and it exfiltrates the non-HttpOnly cookie
Apply the fixes: a CSRF token (or SameSite=Strict) on the update, output-encode the bio everywhere (not just for other viewers), and stop treating self-XSS as unexploitable
flag_hint: The bio is raw on your own /profile but escaped on /u/, and /profile/update?bio= is GET with no CSRF token. POST /report an attacker URL (http://attacker:8080/go?to=>) — the bot's top-level GET nav carries its Lax admin cookie, sets the bio, redirects to /profile where the self-XSS runs and beacons document.cookie. Read /oob/received, POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: self-XSS bio (raw on own /profile, escaped on public /u/<name>) + CSRF-able GET /profile/update (no token)
inspired_by: The classic self-XSS + CSRF escalation chain (a self-only XSS made exploitable by CSRFing the victim's own settings), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask profile app, a mock attacker origin, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
